newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ABN AMRO to push consumer banking in Asia.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to push consumer banking in Asia.

text.p: ABN AMRO Bank plans to make a concerted push to expand its consumer banking operations in Asia, its Asia Pacific chief executive officer, Ton de Boer, said on Thursday.
He told a news conference after the official opening of the bank's new regional head office in Singapore, that it planned to launch consumer banking in Taiwan shortly.
ABN AMRO chairman Jan Kalff said the bank was already an established operator in consumer banking in other parts of the world and would like to make a bigger push in Asia.
"We have an enormous consumer banking operation in the United States. We also have consumer banking operations in other countries.
"It is just that we have hardly done any consumer banking in Asia. We think that there is reason to leverage our capabilities in consumer banking in this part of the world," he said.
ABN AMBRO has some consumer banking operations in India, Pakistan and in Hong Kong but the plan is to make a more "concerted effort" on a regional basis, de Boer said.
The Dutch bank also aims to boost commercial and investment banking as well as treasury operations in Asia.
The new dealing room in the Singapore office, said to be the largest in the city, has 106 positions with room for expansion to 132.
Operational profit before taxes in 1996 for Asia, Australia and Africa was about US$160 million, up 11.5 percent from the previous year.
Kalff said he expected Asia, which contributed about seven percent of group earnings, to continue to post double digit growth rates annually.
Growth would come from the bank's existing businesses as well as by way of selective acquisitions over the coming years, he said.
ABN AMRO was optimistic about Hong Kong, the bank's biggest earner in Asia, after the colony is handed back to China at the end of this month, Kalff said.
ABN AMBRO's merchant banking and stockbroking operations would continue to have their regional headquarters in Hong Kong, he said.
The bank is looking to grow its business in China. "We are already in six cities and have applied for more licenses in China," he said.
